planting.note: Direct sow in warmed soil after the last frost; the short, compact vines and rapid ripening let southern gardeners harvest well ahead of peak late-summer disease and heat stress.

directions: Sow seeds directly in hills once soil has warmed, thinning to two or three vigorous plants per hill spaced roughly three to four feet apart. Racer was developed through a University of New Hampshire and Johnny's Selected Seeds breeding collaboration for exceptionally rapid ripening, producing blocky 12-16 pound fruit with dark green handles well before most other jack-o'-lantern types color up. In Gulf Coast gardens the short vine and early finish are real advantages, letting fruit set and mature before the worst of late-summer humidity drives powdery mildew and vine borer pressure. Harvest once the rind has hardened to a deep, uniform orange and cure in a warm, airy spot for about a week before moving pumpkins to cooler storage.
sources: University of New Hampshire Cooperative Extension

common_name: Camaro PMR Pumpkin (Powdery Mildew Resistant Hybrid Jack-O-Lantern)

planting.note: Direct sow in warm soil after the last frost; built-in powdery mildew resistance is especially valuable in the humid Gulf Coast growing season, when foliar disease usually cuts vines down before fruit finishes sizing.

directions: Direct sow in hills after danger of frost has passed, giving the reduced-vine plants a bit less room than sprawling heirloom types but still allowing air circulation between hills. Camaro PMR carries genetic resistance to powdery mildew, keeping foliage photosynthesizing later into the season so that fruit reaches its full 20-22 pound, near-round, lightly ribbed potential even under heavy disease pressure. The strong handles and deep orange rind make it a reliable choice for growers selling carving pumpkins, and the shorter vine habit suits smaller Gulf Coast garden plots better than old-line field pumpkin types. Watch soil moisture during fruit set, since consistent watering paired with the plant's disease tolerance produces the most uniform, market-ready fruit.
sources: Cornell University Long Island Horticultural Research and Extension Center

common_name: Charisma PMR Pumpkin (Cornell-Bred Powdery Mildew Resistant Jack-O-Lantern)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil is reliably warm; intermediate powdery mildew resistance from Cornell breeding helps this later-maturing pumpkin hold healthy foliage through humid Gulf Coast summers.

directions: Sow directly in hills after the soil has warmed, spacing hills three to four and a half feet apart to give the reduced-length vines room to develop without crowding. Charisma PMR emerged from a joint Cornell University and Johnny's Selected Seeds breeding program and matures a bit later and lighter orange than earlier types like Racer, filling out to 14-18 pounds with a blocky, slightly russeted rind and a slender but sturdy handle. Its intermediate resistance to powdery mildew keeps leaves functional longer into the season, which matters most in regions where warm, humid nights favor the disease. Let fruit color fully and the rind harden before cutting from the vine, leaving several inches of stem attached to prolong storage life.
sources: Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences

common_name: Iron Man Pumpkin (F1 Hard-Shell Personal-Size Pumpkin)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost in full sun; the vigorous, powdery-mildew-tolerant vine and rot-resistant fruit hold up well through a long, muggy Gulf Coast season.

directions: Direct sow in hills once the soil has warmed, allowing the full, vigorous vines plenty of room to run through the second half of the growing season. Iron Man produces round, dark orange fruit only 6-7 inches across and 3-4 pounds, sized for painting projects, porch groupings, and small-space carving rather than large jack-o'-lanterns. The unusually hard rind resists Fusarium and Phytophthora fruit rot, an advantage in the wet, humid soils common along the Gulf Coast, and cured fruit stores for months without softening. Harvest once the shell has fully hardened and cannot be dented with a thumbnail, then cure in a warm, dry spot for a week before moving pumpkins into long-term storage.

common_name: Gladiator Pumpkin (F1 Powdery Mildew Tolerant Jack-O-Lantern)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost in fertile, well-drained soil; intermediate powdery mildew tolerance and firmly rooted handles suit the long, hot, humid pumpkin-growing season along the Gulf Coast.

directions: Sow seeds directly in hills after frost danger has passed, spacing hills widely since Gladiator carries a full, sprawling vine that needs room to support its large fruit load. Fruit grows round to slightly ribbed, deep orange, and sizeable at 20-25 pounds, with a thick, well-anchored handle that stands up to hauling and display without snapping off. Its intermediate resistance to powdery mildew keeps the canopy productive later into the season than older open-pollinated field types, which matters most where warm, humid nights push disease pressure hard in late summer. Cut fruit from the vine with several inches of stem once the rind has hardened and colored fully, then cure before storing in a cool, dry, well-ventilated space.

common_name: Hijinks Pumpkin (AAS-Winning Small Grooved Decorating Pumpkin)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil is warm; notable powdery mildew resistance and a long, vining habit make this a dependable small pumpkin for humid southern gardens.

directions: Direct sow in hills after frost danger passes, giving the long vines, which can reach 15 feet, plenty of open ground or a sturdy trellis to climb. Hijinks was named an All-America Selections winner in 2011 for its unusually uniform 7-9 pound fruit, smooth deep-orange skin with distinctive grooves, and a strong, durable stem that makes an excellent handle. The variety shows notable resistance to powdery mildew and releases cleanly from the vine at harvest, both practical advantages in warm, humid growing regions. Pick once the rind has colored fully and hardened, leaving the handle intact, since Hijinks is prized as much for painting and porch display as for carving.

subcategory: AAS-winning semi-bush jack-o-lantern and baking pumpkin

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost; the semi-bush habit takes noticeably less garden space than sprawling heirloom pumpkins, a real benefit in smaller Gulf Coast vegetable beds.

directions: Sow seeds directly in hills once the soil has warmed, thinning to two or three plants per hill; the compact, semi-bush vine allows closer spacing than traditional long-vined field pumpkins. Spirit was named an All-America Selections winner in 1977 for producing bright orange, deeply oval fruit averaging 10-15 pounds on a plant that stays far more contained than open-pollinated heirlooms. The thick, meaty flesh makes it genuinely dual-purpose, equally suited to a classic jack-o'-lantern face and to being baked down for pumpkin puree. Harvest once the rind has hardened and colored fully, cure briefly in a warm spot, and store in a cool, dry location out of direct sun.

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil is warm; a thick, sturdy stem and solid flesh give this pumpkin good field-storage life through a hot, humid harvest season.

directions: Direct sow in hills after frost danger has passed, spacing hills three to four feet apart to suit the semi-bush growth habit, which takes up markedly less room than sprawling field-pumpkin types. Aspen finishes quickly at around 95 days, producing large, solidly fleshed fruit with a rich orange rind, a thick stem, and handles that hold up well through harvest handling and shipping. Its dense flesh and sturdy rind translate into good post-harvest storage and shipping quality, useful for growers who need fruit to hold up in warm regional markets. Cut fruit with several inches of stem once fully colored and firm, cure in a warm, airy spot, then move to cool, dry storage.
sources: Cornell University Long Island Horticultural Research and Extension Center
